articles.title: Artificial Intelligence giant Anthropic files for Initial Public Offering
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers on Monday (October 26, 2026) for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever, even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.

The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing the SpaceX initial public offering in June that raised a record $86 billion. An Anthropic IPO would also put the company ahead of OpenAI in going public in what is expected to be a pair of blockbuster stock debuts for the rival AI labs.

The filing comes weeks after CEO Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as do its final valuation and offering price, but even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world's most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela, by billions of dollars.

The 335-page document showed Anthropic's revenue is growing rapidly, but like many other tech companies going public, it has yet to turn a profit. The company behind the chatbot Claude reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. That compares to a loss of $13 billion in the same period a year earlier.

Despite the losses, Anthropic, valued earlier this year at $965 billion by private investors, is reportedly set to see that value rise to $1.5 trillion or possibly $2 trillion, although its final valuation has not been established. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would rank among the world's most valuable public companies, alongside Tesla.
As for money raised, the offering could raise as much as $100 billion, according to reports, surpassing the current record set by another one of Musk's companies, SpaceX, earlier this year.
In a regulatory filing, Anthropic said it will list its stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT."
In the filing, the company said it could use some of that money on acquiring other businesses and technology as well as investing in infrastructure to grow its business to take on rivals.
Formed in 2021 by ex-OpenAI leaders, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company and the two leaders, Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, are widely seen as bitter rivals.

But they have plenty of other competitors, including Google, newer startups in the U.S. and China and Musk's SpaceX, which has an AI business. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX's AI division have all been losing more money than they make because of the huge costs in resources in building AI, fueling concerns of a bubble.

The IPO would help cover any cash shortfall as well as shower extraordinary wealth on Anthropic's seven founders, including Amodei and his sister. Collectively they own nearly 500 million shares, though it's unclear from the offering document how much that will represent of the company after the IPO.

The filing also listed a host of risks for the San Francisco-based Anthropic, ranging from not being able to retain key staff, navigate regulatory roadblocks and secure enough compute power to run its AI systems.

articles.title: UN-commissioned experts say Gaza ceasefire has not stopped Israel from committing genocide
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A ceasefire agreement in Gaza has not stopped what a group of independent experts commissioned by the UN say is genocide carried out by Israel in the territory, the team said in a new report on Monday (October 26, 2026). They also accused Israeli forces of crimes against humanity, including torture and rape, in the West Bank.
Israel, which denies both the genocide and the sexual assault claims, did not immediately respond to the report's publication.

The Associated Press could not independently corroborate multiple graphic accounts described in the report of sexual assaults by prison guards and soldiers on Palestinian detainees since October 2023. In one, female guards strip-searched a pregnant Palestinian woman. .In another, guards beat and hurled sexist slurs while denying a detainee access to the toilet and sanitary pads. She bled onto her clothes and interrogation chair.

The findings by the Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which seeks to document in minute detail the allegations and evidence of crimes to bolster accountability for perpetrators, could be used by prosecutors at the International Criminal Court or in other jurisdictions to try to bring justice to victims and their relatives.
The report on Monday (October 26) said Israel was “continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza.”

The report also accused Israel and members of its security forces of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the West Bank and Gaza, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence and persecution against civilians. File | Photo Credit: AP

Much of the harm has come, the report says, from Israel's expansion deeper into Gaza during that period. Since October 2025, when the ceasefire was signed, Israeli forces have gone from controlling 53% of Gaza to at least 60%, the commission said.
In that time, Israeli fire across the advancing front has killed at least 196 Palestinians – including 18 women, 32 boys and 11 girls.

The report also accused Israel and members of its security forces of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the West Bank and Gaza, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence and persecution against civilians.

The commission said that it had recently documented six cases where Israeli guards were sexually violent toward male detainees from Gaza in the Sde Teiman military prison. In one case, it says guards raped a Palestinian detainee.

The commission says it drew its conclusions after investigating seven cases between November 2023 and June 2026, where Israeli forces caused bodily harm to Palestinians, often children, who did not appear to be posing a threat.

articles.title: Protests in France | Beginning of the end of Macronism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: France is in turmoil. More than half a million people hit the streets on October 17, as protests swept across the country. As the administration greeted the protesters with a large deployment of riot police, peaceful demonstrations were engulfed by violence in many places. Arsonists set fire to the Lyon tourist office and burnt down the Limoges City Hall, a historic municipal building. Protesters stormed the townhall in Marseille and attacked the prefect’s residence in Bordeaux. In Paris’s Place de la Republique, protesting youth who clashed with the police torched vehicles and looted shops. Luxury retailers such as Louis Vuitton, Hermes, Dior and Galeries Lafayette suffered millions of dollars in losses as their stores were ransacked. Police arrested or detained more than 6,000 people, including hundreds of minors.

With the police outnumbered and unable to protect public and private property, several cities resorted to full or partial curfews. Government officials have blamed the unrest on “seditionists from far-left fringe groups”. They have accused La France Insoumise, or LFI (France Unbowed), the leftwing political party launched by veteran politician Jean-Luc Melenchon (75), of inciting the protests with the aim of extracting political mileage ahead of the presidential elections in April 2027.

articles.title: U.K. PM Burnham backs principle of ‘earned settlement’ in immigration rules
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that he stands by the principle that settlement (permanent residence) in the U.K. should be “earned” and not granted automatically. An increase in the baseline qualifying period for settlement, from 5 of 15 years had been proposed by U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood as part of a draft “earned settlement” immigration overhaul last year, during the Keir Starmer administration. Individuals could qualify for shorter or longer periods depending on income, immigration violations and other factors.

Indian citizens are likely to be significantly impacted by the new rules. Indian nationals constituted the largest group from outside the EU + (EU and a few other European countries) area to migrate long-term to the U.K. for the year ending December 2025.

“We’ll set out the plan on that quite soon,” Mr. Burnham said during a TV interview on Monday (October 26, 2026) morning. He said the government was still considering the responses received in the public consultation process that took place earlier this year. In recent weeks the Prime Minister has indicated that the government would soften the proposed stance towards social care workers. These individuals formed a significant part of the ‘Boriswave’ of migration – a surge in migrants in the early 2020s - who are now becoming eligible for settlement.

Mr. Burnham said that since the U.K. left the E.U. in 2016, things had not “played out as people said it would at the time” with the country’s economy weakening and control over immigration becoming more challenging. He said “revolving-door immigration” was being replaced by permanent immigration to the U.K.
Over the weekend, the Sunday Times had reported that Mr. Burnham had told the publication that he would be open to considering ‘free movement’ (i.e., right to live and work) between the U.K. and E.U.
In his Monday (October 26, 2026) interview, Mr. Burnham reiterated his wish to see the U.K. rejoin the E.U. in his lifetime, adding, however, that would “not move ahead of the public”.

“The British public …will be the bosses here. They will decide what will happen in relation to Brexit,” he said, as he denied that he was “testing the waters” with the public and media on how a return to the E.U. would be received.
The U.K. and EU are working towards concluding an agreement that would cover agriculture and immigration among other areas, at a summit meeting on November 20.
Mr. Burnham ruled out an early general election. The current parliament expires in 2029.

articles.title: Lula wins a record fourth presidential term as Brazil defeats far-right, defies Trump and Meta
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: In an election campaign that may be recorded in history for countering far-right tactics, defying foreign interference and social media manipulation, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro of Liberal Party (PL) in Brazil’s runoff elections on Sunday (October 25, 2026). Mr. Lula secured 64 million votes, the highest total ever recorded in a Brazilian presidential election, surpassing his own record of 60 million votes he received in 2022.

Declaring a “defeat for lies and denialism”, he pledged to govern for all Brazilians and protect the country’s sovereignty. “Brazil is nobody’s backyard,” Mr. Lula declared at a midnight rally, sending a clear message to U.S. president Donald Trump as he addressed hundreds of thousands of supporters gathered along São Paulo’s iconic Avenida Paulista.

In an emotional speech, Mr. Lula thanked women and older voters for their support and praised the mobilisation of young people on the streets and on social media. “People went out to vote because we managed to convince them that their votes were extremely important to safeguarding democracy in the country,” he said. He also said he had learned many lessons from the election and promised to change his approach to governing, ensure greater public participation in government decisions and give digital communication a more prominent role during his fourth term. “The future begins today, and its name is youth. I salute the women who made all the difference. I salute the older people who made sacrifices and made their way to the polling stations to vote,” he said.

Mr. Lula secured an unprecedented comeback in the election. He trailed in the first round, receiving 45.16% of valid votes against 47.03% for Mr. Flávio. As the prospect of a Bolsonaro presidency caused a major concern among the young, especially about public education, healthcare and transport, millions of people joined weekly rallies across the country, pledging support for Mr. Lula and demanding protection of public services. On Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Lula told his young supporters that their voices have been heard. “We will make increasing investment in in the Unified Health System, develop a national artificial intelligence system, continue to expand public universities and support the digital and creative economies,” Mr. Lula told his supporters with massive rounds of applause.

The turnaround after the first round of election on October 4 was not only historic but also dramatic. Mr. Lula’s official campaign team almost took a back seat as millions of people came out on streets and joined the social media campaign. The online mobilisation was led by federal deputy André Janones, who is not a member of the Workers Party but created a WhatsApp channel called “Lula’s Army”, where he issued “missions” to more than 10 million subscribers every day. The campaign focused its efforts on persuading undecided voters and those who had abstained in the first round. Mr. Lula’s young supporters, many of them teenagers, went on door-to-door campaigns to win over voters who had backed other candidates in the first round. On Sunday (October 25, 2026), abstention rates fell to their lowest levels since 2002.

With most opinion polls predicting a neck-to-neck race and some even giving an edge to Mr. Flavio till a few days back, the Workers’ Party shifted its messaging from a comparison of the candidates’ personal records to a forward-looking agenda centred on concrete promises. Following the first-round results, Mr. Lula changed his campaign team’s leadership and began announcing measures such as an increase in direct cash transfer benefits, a new debt-relief programme, a package of benefits for small entrepreneurs and a pledge to make public transport free on weekends.

Even as Mr. Lula made these promises to the electorate, his campaign faced a big challenge: Big Tech firms – from Meta to X and Google – openly supported Mr. Flavio’s campaign while suppressing advertising by Mr. Lula’s team. In his speech on Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Lula said he had to overcome “interference” by digital platforms and pledged to regulate big tech companies in Brazil. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference coming from outside and through digital platforms. We will have to regulate them,” Mr. Lula said. On October 16 after an expose in the Brazilian media, Meta had admitted that its artificial intelligence tool had blocked the generation of campaign material supporting Mr. Lula while allowing the same technology to be used by the Flávio campaign.

With this historic mobilisation of people and a record victory, Mr. Lula also seems to have defeated Mr. Trump, who has repeatedly made clear that his preferred candidate in the race was Mr. Flávio. Now, Mr. Lula’s victory has applied brakes on the growing wave of right-wing leaders in the region. But Mr. Trump is not in a mood to throw in the towel. On Sunday (October 25, 2026) night, Mr. Trump questioned Mr. Lula’s victory, comparing it to the 2020 U.S. election which he lost to Joe Biden and alleged that Brazil had followed the “Joe Biden playbook.”

“Bolsonaro had a big lead in the first round and was the clear favourite to win the second. But the communists never give up power once they get it,” Mr. Trump said, echoing the far-right’s strategy of questioning election results which do not go in their favour.

Mr. Flávio was singing the same tune on Sunday (October 25, 2026) night as he refused to accept the election result, announcing that he would seek the annulment of the election. He accused the Federal Supreme Federal of “changing the rules midway” after a judge ordered voting across the country to be extended until 7 p.m. when Mr. Lula complained about many right-wing mayors curtailing the bus services in the poor areas many cities. “It is impossible to recognise the election result in the context in which these things happened,” Mr. Flavio said, adding that his legal team would challenge the outcome.

It is a complete misreading of the mood in Brazil. After Mr. Lula finished his speech on Sunday (October 25, 2026) night, the crowd broke into a rendition of Brazil’s national independence song, sending a message to the far-right, Mr. Trump and Meta.

Supporters of Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the Workers' Party (PT) candidate for re-election, react to early result during the presidential runoff election, in Sao Paulo, Brazil on October 25, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

articles.title: Why West Bengal’s C-Sections, at nearly 1 in 2 births, demand a hard look
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: On September 29, 2015, a memo went out from Swasthya Bhawan, the West Bengal Health Department’s headquarters in Salt Lake, to every medical college principal and every district’s chief medical officer of health. Its subject was a concern the Union Health Ministry had raised about rising Caesarean sections rates, especially where the operation was not medically needed.

The memo enclosed a statement the World Health Organization (WHO) had issued that April. It suggested that chief medical officers, who license private clinics, carry out periodic “prescription audits” of Caesareans in private and government facilities.

At the time, the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4, 2015-16) had found that about one in four births were Caesareans in West Bengal (23.8%). The latest sixth round (NFHS-6, 2023-24) puts the figure at 44.5%, close to double that level, against 27.2% for India. In Kolkata and North 24 Parganas it was found to be 67.5%, meaning about two of every three babies were born via a C-section.

A Caesarean section saves mothers and babies when labour goes wrong. It is also, however, major abdominal surgery, with slower recovery rates and higher risks of infection and bleeding, and it leaves a scar that can complicate later pregnancies.

The WHO statement said that across a population, Caesarean rates above 10% are not associated with fewer deaths of mothers or newborns. While the WHO does not recommend a specific rate , the increasing numbers of Caesarean births in West Bengal, and more widely in India, deserve attention.
The NFHS’s first three rounds, from 1992-93 to 2005-06, found West Bengal close to the national average when it came to C-sections, at 10.2% against 8.5% by the third NFHS round.

The State then pulled away. Its rate reached 32.6% in NFHS-5, for which West Bengal was surveyed in 2019-21, and by NFHS-6 (2023-24) the gap with India had widened from 1.7 percentage points in 2005-06 to 17.3.
The climb has also grown steeper. The rise of 13.6 points between 2005-06 and 2015-16 took a decade, while the latest 11.9 points came in four to five years.
The data cannot reveal how many of West Bengal’s operations were necessary, though it does show when and where the rise happened.

Of every 10 women who give birth in a private facility in West Bengal, 9 nine now have a C-section (87.7%). In 2015-16, the year of the memo, the figure was 70.9%. West Bengal’s numbers are also significantly higher than current the national private-sector rate, 54.1%.

While numbers in the government sector are lower, they are also on the rise: government facilities performed C-sections in 28.8% of the births they handled, up from 18.8% in 2015-16 and 1.7 times the national public-sector figure of 16.9%. In Kolkata, the share of births in government facilities delivered by C-section rose from 32.4% in NFHS-5 to 59.1% in NFHS-6.
Births are also increasingly moving to private facilities. Between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 their share of the total rose from about 19% to about 29%, even as the public share fell from 72.4% to 65.8%.

articles.title: Amgen drug combined with immunotherapy extends survival in lung cancer trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Amgen's Imdelltra used in combination with ​AstraZeneca's immunotherapy Imfinzi reduced the risk of death by 58% compared ⁠to the Astra drug alone in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, according to data from a study presented at a major medical meeting on Saturday.
Imfinzi is currently the standard of care following chemotherapy ‌for patients with this very aggressive and hard-to-treat disease whose cancer does not worsen after initial chemotherapy.
The study found that those given both drugs ‌lived for a median of 21.1 months, compared with 12.7 months for those treated only ‌with ⁠Imfinzi.

"If you give Imdelltra earlier and earlier, you get bigger clinical benefit," ⁠said Paul Burton, chief medical officer at California-based Amgen. He called the results "unprecedented in advancing the treatment of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer."
Imdelltra's U.S. list price is about $30,000 per cycle, or over $390,000 a year. Wall Street analysts ​have estimated annual sales reaching more ‌than $2.5 billion by 2030, according to LSEG data.

The Amgen drug is currently approved for adults in the advanced stages of small cell lung cancer that has worsened despite chemotherapy, based on data showing that Imdelltra reduced the risk of death by 40%.

Full results ‌of the 563-patient trial were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology ​meeting in Madrid and published in the New England Journal of Medicine . Amgen had previously announced that the Phase 3 study was successful.

Imdelltra ⁠belongs to a dual-target class of drugs called bispecific antibodies designed to pull immune system T cells into contact with cancer cells to destroy them. Imfinzi is an older type of ‌immunotherapy that essentially blocks the mechanism tumors use to hide from immune-system assault.

Most lung cancer cases are non-small cell, while up to 15% are the small cell variety targeted by Imdelltra. About 250,000 new cases are diagnosed worldwide each year, according to the U.S. National Institutes of Health.
Very few people diagnosed with small cell lung cancer are candidates for surgery, and most are initially given radiotherapy and chemotherapy, Burton said.
Survival rates depend on ‌when the cancer is diagnosed, but the overall 5-year rate is only around 9%, according to the American ​Cancer Society.
Amgen said that nearly 80% of trial patients treated with the combination were alive after one year, compared with 53% of those on Imfinzi ⁠alone, as patient follow-up continues.

articles.title: IIT Bombay develops low-cost device to screen for anaemia, sickle cell disease
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Indian Institute of Technology Bombay on Friday said its researchers have developed a low-cost device that can screen for anaemia and sickle cell disease using a drop of blood.

A research team from the Department of Chemical Engineering, led by Mahesh Tirumkudulu, has developed a simple, low-cost point-of-care approach that uses the length of a blood smear (the distance that a drop of blood spreads across a glass slide) to detect anaemia, and detect and monitor treatment for sickle cell disease. IIT Bombay said.

Prof Tirumkudulu's team built their own automated device to have a uniform method of creating a smear. Under these controlled conditions, the researchers observed that blood from different people gives different smear lengths, and this difference holds useful information.
Prof. Tirumkudulu explained that more viscous blood spreads less easily and, therefore, produces a shorter and thicker smear under the same conditions.

Once the team confirmed that the method could sense small differences in blood viscosity, they decided to investigate whether those differences could help identify disease. It was found that anaemia lowers red blood cell concentration and haemoglobin, while sickle cell disease makes red blood cells rigid.

The researchers said their patented automated smearing device can be manufactured cost-effectively. Also, the test itself requires only a pipette, glass slides, an inexpensive chemical, vials for the sickling treatment, and a ruler or imaging device to measure smear length, they added.

"This makes our technique particularly useful in places where conventional diagnostic laboratories are difficult to access, and it doesn't require any special expertise to use," said Dr. Mahrukh Mir, a former PhD scholar in Prof Tirumkudulu's lab, and the first author of the study.
The researchers pointed out that blood viscosity cutoffs vary for various groups of people because certain genetic differences affect how blood reacts when oxygen levels drop.

Also, the anaemia test could miss identifying some patients when the usual link between viscosity and anaemia does not hold, such as in a rare condition called hyperviscosity syndrome, where blood plasma is unusually thick.

Currently, the technology is licensed to Rheoheme Private Limited, an IIT Bombay startup, and the team is now working with the National Institute for Research in Tribal Health, Jabalpur, in Madhya Pradesh and All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Nagpur, toward regulatory approval, while exploring extending the device to measure clotting time and glucose levels.
"Our initial aim was to understand the physics of spreading blood drop, and that led to the medical applications," added Prof Tirumkudulu.

articles.title: Most people globally face 'high genetic risk' for three common diseases: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Most people worldwide could be categorised as having a high genetic risk for three of 28 common conditions, including diabetes, cardiovascular disease and schizophrenia, even if they might not develop them, a new study has found.

Researchers, led by the UK's University of Exeter, described the 'average' human genome, finding that everyone, regardless of their current health status, could be considered at risk for numerous conditions based on their genetics alone.

Every person's genome, or the average human genome, contains around five million variants, or DNA locations that differ between individuals, the findings published in the journal Genome Medicine reveal.

The locations include around 10,000 variants that alter gene sequences, which can have positive or negative effect, ranging from lactose intolerance to drug response, though are often biologically neutral, they show.

Each person also carries between one and three rare variants previously shown to cause serious genetic diseases, and another 50 rare variants that are currently of uncertain clinical relevance, the researchers found.
The team analysed data from two major population biobanks -- the UK Biobank and the US' All of Us -- that include whole genome sequencing, covering nearly one million individuals.

Senior author Caroline Wright, from the University of Exeter, said, "Whole genome sequencing has become such an important tool in diagnosing genetic disease, and we're increasingly moving towards genetic screening for predicting disease."

"Yet most people are unaware of just how much genetic variation is present in every genome. Actually, variation is the norm. For the first time, our study outlines what to expect in the average human genome, which can benefit clinicians and patients across the word in understanding, interpreting and contextualising genomics," Wright said.
The researchers also analysed numerous polygenic risk scores, which consider all known genetic factors to calculate a person's future risk of developing a disease.

"... applying polygenic scores (PGS) for 28 common diseases within UKB (UK Biobank), we estimate that the average person is in the top 10 per cent for (nearly) three conditions, and around one in five people are in the top one per cent for at least one PGS," the authors wrote.
"Importantly, we found that everyone carries a small number of genetic variants linked to disease, although many of these will not actually cause disease in that individual," Wright said.

The senior author added, "It is therefore crucial to consider context when interpreting findings from genetic testing, including symptoms or family history of disease as well as other clinical and environmental risk factors. Our findings also provide important context for professionals who are interpreting genetic testing results or commissioning genetic screening programmes."

articles.title: Bengaluru’s BMTC drivers, traffic police, pourakarmikas, construction workers show reduced lung function: Survey
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A three-year long study in Bengaluru of over 10,000 frontline workers has brought to light reduced lung function among BMTC bus drivers, traffic police, pourakarmikas and construction workers — sections most exposed to polluted air.

The study, done by the VAAYU Occupational & Environmental Respiratory Illness Clinic (VOERIC), screened 4,517 BMTC drivers, 3,285 traffic police personnel, 2,169 construction workers and 379 pourakarmikas.
A traffic policeman wears a mask at a traffic signal in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: BHAGYA PRAKASH
All the groups that were screened showed higher-than-normal prevalence of early lung-function abnormalities.

Among the occupations, pourakarmikas were found to have the highest proportion of workers with the PRISm pattern, an indication of reduced lung capacity. Around 45% of them showed indications of reduced lung function.
BMTC workers and traffic police followed, with 29.5% and 28%, respectively, showing reduced lung function. Among construction workers, 15% showed a PRISm pattern.
Around 2.6% of BMTC drivers, 2.3% pourakarmikas, 2.1% construction workers, and 1% traffic police personnel reported signs of obstructive airflow.
The survey also found that 88.2% of the BMTC drivers never used a mask, as was the case with 55% traffic police, 37.9% construction workers, and 16.3% pourakarmikas.
Workers breaking stones during pipeline work at Race Course in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: SUDHAKARA JAIN
The subjects were also analysed for comorbidities, and the results revealed a grim situation, with high levels of obesity reported among the sections.
Pourakarmikas had the highest proportion at 62%, closely followed by BMTC drivers, 60.7% of whom were found to be obese/overweight. For traffic police, the figure stood at 51.3%.
The figures are much higher than the India reference figure of 28.6%.

articles.title: Gujarat govt. declares Devbhoomi Dwarka, Kutch, Jamnagar and Porbandar as drought-affected
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Gujarat government on Monday (October 26, 2026) declared Devbhoomi Dwarka, Kutch, Jamnagar and Porbandar districts as drought-affected.

Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel said the decision on drought declaration was taken as per the guidelines of the Centre after monsoon ended in the state. As per the Centre's 2016 guideline on drought, the announcement will be in effect for six months, Mr. Patel added.

"The state has received 89% rain this monsoon. However, Devbhoomi Dwarka, Kutch, Jamnagar and Porbandar received very little rain. So these four districts have been declared drought-affected," Mr. Patel told reporters.
The State government will stand with farmers during these difficult times, he added.

"The state government will give assistance under SDRF (State Disaster Response Fund) of ₹8,500 per hectare for two hectares to farmers whose crops have failed. The state government has already started providing fodder at discounted rates of ₹2 per kilo," Mr. Patel said.

"The Gujarat government will provide ₹80 per cattle to cattle shelters for upkeep of the animals. It will also provide 150 days of employment under VB-G RAM G (Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) ) in affected districts. This will be implemented from November 1," Mr. Patel said.
The state government, under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, will always remain with farmers and people and take decisions in their favour, Mr. Patel asserted.

articles.title: Old values, new avenues: On India-Poland ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Sixteen years after his visit as Poland’s Prime Minister, Donald Tusk’s travel to Delhi and Bengaluru last week was to signal a renewed desire to work closely with India. Mr. Tusk’s visit, two months ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to Brussels to sign the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement , indicated one part of his agenda. Both sides agreed that it was time to develop trade, currently worth just $6 billion, to double its size by 2030. Mr. Tusk’s last visit to India was in 2017, as President of the European Council for the EU-India summit, and it is fitting that his trip was just as the FTA is finalised and ratified after years of delays. Another area of increased India-Poland collaboration is in technology, AI and defence hardware, critical minerals, renewable and nuclear energy given Poland’s expertise in the last few decades and India’s capacity for scale. As the EU’s sixth largest economy, Poland has officially crossed the $1 trillion GDP (nominal terms) milestone. Its $120-billion-dollar tech economy is also gaining global interest. A large part of Polish machinery and parts is exported to Germany, which in turn has a growing share of Indian imports, and India could consider more trilateral collaborations for manufacturing and mining technology. The two sides agreed to establish a “Defence Industry Dialogue” and explore a dialogue on counter-terrorism cooperation. Finally, the Modi-Tusk talks focused on geopolitics, particularly the ongoing war in Ukraine. The war’s impact, especially on the Global South, has been a concern for India, and the Modi government’s initiative to work on an agreement acceptable to Kyiv and Moscow on grain exports and seafarers’ safety was discussed. The four-pronged plan, announced by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar during his September visit to Warsaw, won Mr. Tusk’s support.

At the India-Poland Business Forum in Bengaluru, Mr. Tusk, who was accompanied by a Polish business delegation, said the challenge now was in “translating” the talks and MoUs signed into actual joint ventures between businesses. Apart from the distance and geographies, there is the matter of trust, given India’s defence engagement with Russia and Poland’s defence ties with Pakistan. Poland is credited with training Pakistan’s Air Force in its early years; a mutual defence cooperation agreement was signed in 2018. India has a unique and enduring partnership with Russia, and New Delhi is unlikely to accept Warsaw’s strictures over its military engagement and exercises with Russia that caused a controversy earlier this year during the Polish Foreign Minister’s visit. It is essential for Delhi and Warsaw to complete the confidentiality of classified information that is still being negotiated and draw up the parameters of future cooperation based on realities. Mr. Tusk’s statement that India and Poland today have no “conflicts of interest” is a significant aspiration, for two countries that share old values, and new avenues of partnership.

articles.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. Associated with the heating up of the Central Pacific, the El Niño is linked to the drying up of the southwest monsoon rains but also yoked — not always — with a vigorous northeast monsoon. Other than in 2015, several El Niño years, such as 1997 and 2009, have been associated with above-normal rainfall between October and December in Tamil Nadu though El Niño years, such as 2002 and 1982, saw a poor northeast monsoon (and a predictably bad southwest monsoon). While the climate mechanisms linking a vigorous northeast monsoon and El Niño are still to be fully understood, it appears the warming patterns of the El Niño tend to deflect rain-bearing cyclonic circulations in unpredictable ways. Therefore, the Centre and the southern States ought to take enough precautions: from clearing up stormwater drains, fortifying shelters, making provisions for infrastructure damage and tightening weather warning forecasts to prepare for torrents.

articles.title: In the crossfire: on India and the Saudi-Houthi conflict
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The killing of an Indian national in a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Dammam airport is a grim reminder of the dangers the kingdom’s Indian community faces as the conflict between Riyadh and Yemen’s Shia militants escalates. Since the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis resumed in July, at least two Indians have been killed and 14 others wounded. On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that a yacht with 14 Indians was targeted by Saudi forces near Yemen’s Zuqar island in the Red Sea and that rescue operations were under way. As the Houthis, who control parts of Northern Yemen and its entire Red Sea coast, step up attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports, Indians, who are the kingdom’s largest expat community, risk getting caught in the crossfire. With flights disrupted, thousands of Indian pilgrims are stranded. India has condemned Houthi attacks, saying that it “stands in solidarity” with Saudi Arabia. With no end in sight to the fighting and a high possibility of Israel and the U.S. resuming their Iran strikes, further violence and instability in West Asia could make India’s choices increasingly difficult.

The Saudi-Houthi conflict dates back to the Houthi takeover of Sana’a, Yemen’s capital, in 2014. A year later, Saudi Arabia began bombing Yemen to drive the Houthis out. But years of Saudi bombing of one of the poorest Arab countries have proved counterproductive; the Houthis consolidated support among the tribes of northern Yemen and built a powerful territorial army and naval force. The Saudi-Houthi ceasefire of 2022 collapsed in July 2026 after Saudi Arabia recklessly bombed Sana’a airport, to prevent an Iranian plane with a Houthi delegation from landing. The Houthis subsequently began attacking Saudi Arabia’s critical infrastructure, and launched a ground offensive against the Saudi-backed forces in Yemen. The Houthi attacks pose the biggest security challenge to Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince and the main architect of the war on Yemen, in decades. Massive Saudi air strikes have neither defeated the Houthis nor restored the kingdom’s deterrence. With its wealth, natural resources, infrastructure and tenuous palace politics, the kingdom remains exposed to Houthi missile and drone attacks, with few good options for a way out. India must prepare a contingency plan for worst-case scenarios. Its immediate priority should be to evacuate stranded Indian pilgrims. It should also articulate a stronger position for stability and work with Arab countries and Tehran to push for a diplomatic settlement to the Iran crisis . For peace to prevail in the Persian Gulf, the guns directed at Iran must first fall silent.

• The killing of an Indian national in a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia’s Dammam airport is a grim reminder of the dangers the kingdom’s Indian community faces as the conflict between Riyadh and Yemen’s Shia militants escalates. Since the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis resumed in July, at least two Indians have been killed and 14 others wounded. On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that a yacht with 14 Indians was targeted by Saudi forces near Yemen’s Zuqar island in the Red Sea and that rescue operations were under way. As the Houthis, who control parts of Northern Yemen and its entire Red Sea coast, step up attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including oil facilities and airports, Indians, who are the kingdom’s largest expat community, risk getting caught in the crossfire. With flights disrupted, thousands of Indian pilgrims are stranded. India has condemned Houthi attacks, saying that it “stands in solidarity” with Saudi Arabia. With no end in sight to the fighting and a high possibility of Israel and the U.S. resuming their Iran strikes, further violence and instability in West Asia could make India’s choices increasingly difficult.

But years of Saudi bombing of one of the poorest Arab countries have proved counterproductive; the Houthis consolidated support among the tribes of northern Yemen and built a powerful territorial army and naval force. articles.title: Falling short: on Marco Rubio’s second visit to India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The United States Secretary of State’s three-day visit to India , his second in five months, came at a significant time in U.S. politics. Marco Rubio’s Mumbai trip this week was just ahead of the U.S. midterm elections , which would mark the midpoint of President Donald Trump’s second term in office — a point at which the incumbent normally begins to focus on legacy, and possible contenders for the next Presidential election (Mr. Rubio is expected to be one), and start to look for possible partners and friendships around the world. In addition, his visit also raised hopes in New Delhi of a reset in bilateral ties, battered by two years of uncertainty over the Trump administration’s actions. This would include positive moves towards concluding the Bilateral Trade Agreement , reassuring India about U.S. sanctions on the import of Russian oil, preparations for upcoming Trump meets with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Manila (ASEAN) and Miami (G-20) summits, discussing plans for the Quad Summit (on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit) that India has been trying to host, and setting a date for Mr. Trump’s India visit. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s invitation also offered Mr. Rubio an opportunity to meet their UAE counterpart, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, to discuss the Gulf situation and to restore energy security and connectivity. And finally, Mr. Rubio’s visit to the Jamnagar Reliance refinery, led to speculation of some major deals on energy, possibly offering more discounts as he pitched for India to buy more American and U.S.-licensed Venezuelan oil.

Given all the high expectations, the visit was bound to come up short. The optics of his visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar, but not New Delhi, which was announced by the U.S. Ambassador to India , gave the Opposition fodder to question the real purpose of the visit. Despite Mr. Rubio’s two visits to India and more than six by Mr. Jaishankar to the U.S. since Mr. Trump took office, relations remain on edge, with issues on trade, tariffs, H-1B restrictions and anti-immigrant measures unaddressed. Also, the U.S.’s narrative on Operation Sindoor (2025), growing ties with Pakistan, and the Trump administration’s rhetoric on India’s economy, diaspora and Russian oil trade have added to India’s unhappiness. The two sides did not announce any agreements and Mr. Jaishankar and Mr. Rubio did not hold a joint press address. However, as they did at the U.S. Independence Day’s 250th anniversary celebrations in Delhi in May, they attended the “Freedom 250” event in Mumbai. Mr. Rubio acknowledged that while no two countries would agree on all issues, he said the U.S.-India alignment on core issues of national interest was “extraordinary” . From this point on, Mr. Rubio must walk that talk, with a view to ensuring that India-U.S. ties are able to move on from the difficulties of the last few years.

articles.title: Canary in the coal mine: On the performance of India’s core industrial sectors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The latest data on the performance of the core industrial sectors show the economy may be facing an industrial uptick, but questions about its sustainability remain. Growth in the Index of Core Industries rose to a series-high of 7.9% in September 2026, the second consecutive month of accelerated performance. Any such improvement is to be celebrated, but a deeper look at what is driving it is also warranted. The coal sector saw growth suddenly shoot up to 10.7% in September. The unexpected and unusual nature of this rapid acceleration can be borne out by the fact that the sector contracted by 1.1% over the longer April-September 2026 period. The growth in coal in September was likely a temporary blip aided by a statistical low base and, more importantly, pressure from power plant operators over rapidly depleting coal stocks amid the heat wave. The electricity sector grew 11.4% in September, capping off a half-year dominated by double-digit growth. This surge in electricity-related demand for coal will likely wane, especially since the El Niño factor that drove the heat wave will also result in a milder winter. The other sector that results in high coal usage, the steel sector, did accelerate in September, but not by enough to sustain the coal sector’s September output. The uptick in steel did, however, result in a return to double-digit growth for the iron ore sector, which should bode well for the mining component of the larger Index of Industrial Production.

The performance of the crude oil, natural gas, and refinery products sectors also highlights the fiscal problems India faces. At a time when the crude oil and natural gas sectors have both contracted continuously since 2024, refinery output rose to 10.3% in September. This means that the refineries were increasingly processing expensive imported oil. India’s oil imports in September were up 7% by volume but jumped 47% in terms of value due to the high price of oil. This is set to worsen. The attacks on Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure have already pushed global oil prices above $112 a barrel, almost a six-month high. The reprieve from the U.S. on potential tariffs linked to imports of Russian oil provide India a reliable source, but the days of discounts are long gone. It is the time of premium pricing, and each barrel imported is eating into India’s foreign exchange reserves, which are also being used to defend the rupee. Cement and steel are the only sustainably growing core sectors, and those too are based on government infrastructure spending. At a time when industrial output is only temporarily propped up, the government’s fiscal space is fast shrinking.

articles.title: Tunnelling through: On China’s export control list, tunnel-boring machines
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Chinese Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs decision to place tunnel-boring machines (TBMs) on an export control list reveals a blind spot in India’s supply chain diversification. The curbs include TBMs, walking excavators, and high-altitude wet shotcrete machines. From November 18, if a shipment is intended for countries or regions deemed sensitive due to ongoing disputes with China, exporters will need an export licence from commerce authorities. For other countries/regions, exporters will need to be registered, obtain an export certificate, and submit end-use declarations stating that the equipment will not be re-routed to sensitive locations. While China has cornered around 70% of the global TBM market, prominent manufacturers in the West also maintain substantial component supply chains in the country to cut manufacturing overhead. Further, TBMs are complex to build as they have to be configured to geological characteristics at the project site and perform numerous tasks. Where a suitable TBM exists, it can be used for civilian or military purposes. India has struggled with TBM-related hold-ups with China for at least two years now, including for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail project. Germany’s Herrenknecht AG set up an assembling and refurbishing facility in Chennai in 2007-08. TBM production economics differ significantly from conventional construction equipment as new plants need a minimum number of orders and must be able to access the industrial capability required to design, manufacture and repair specialised components.

However, even though India is one of the world’s largest TBM importers, expecting every sophisticated machine to be produced domestically will send public infrastructure costs soaring. Even now, depending on China’s decision on the TBMs set for India, India may have to redirect its procurement to facilities based directly in Germany or Japan, say, and absorb the higher capital cost. The BEML experience shows that manufacturing partnerships can fail without secure licensing arrangements and access to sustained demand. India should pursue domestic manufacturing alongside international partnerships, e.g., making equipment in the country under agreement with established foreign firms, and develop shared industrial capabilities rather than singular ‘national champions’, as TBM manufacturers and their suppliers can benefit from access to common testing and precision manufacturing infrastructure. Overall, Beijing is systematically identifying sectors where it commands a significant global capacity and establishing export controls to counter western technological restrictions, such as on advanced semiconductors, so any critical infrastructure sector relying on Chinese supply lines will face a compounding geopolitical risk.

articles.title: Kuttiadi eyes river circuit to tap tourism potential
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Tourism department and the Kozhikode district administration are considering a proposal to develop a river tourism circuit connecting local bodies through which the Kuttiadi river flows, with a view to promoting river and hill tourism in the Kuttiadi Assembly constituency.

A meeting chaired by Kuttiadi MLA Parakkal Abdulla was recently held to discuss the proposal. The MLA submitted a comprehensive report on the tourism potential of rivers, ponds, paddy fields and hills in the constituency to District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty, with the aim of promoting the region’s overall development.
The meeting decided to organise a joint river expedition involving the District Collector, the MLA, grama panchayat presidents and tourism officials to explore the region’s tourism potential.

The proposed projects include a heritage walking trail and a happiness park in Kuttiadi; birdwatching, farm tourism and a walkway at Cherandathur Chira; kayaking and ecotourism on the Chovva river; and a tourism project at Thuruthi–Perinchery Kadavu along with a bamboo park in Thiruvallur.

A team of experts from the Tourism department is expected to visit the proposed locations soon to assess their feasibility. A team led by the District Collector will subsequently visit the shortlisted sites.
The meeting also decided to take urgent steps to improve facilities at Payamkuttimala and widen the road leading to the hill.

The district will host various programmes until November 2 as part of the anti-corruption awareness campaign.

A walkathon was also organised near the Civil Station in association with the Malappuram Runners Club. Deputy Collector (Disaster Management) Swathi Chandramohan flagged off the walkathon.

articles.title: Suspected kingpin of drug network held in Malappuram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A special police team arrested Ibrahim Badusha, 29, alleged kingpin of a drug trafficking network operating across Keralam and other States, from a hideout at Kolathur in Malappuram district on Monday (October 26).

A native of Kadambode, Panthalloor, Mr. Badusha is suspected of playing a key role in the network linked to the seizure of 12.8 kg of MDMA from Coimbatore. The police had arrested three men with the drugs, valued at more than ₹10 crore in the retail market, concealed in the door panels of a car, in August this year.

The seizure followed an investigation into a drug network exposed after six people were arrested with 100 gm of suspected MDMA from a private apartment in Manjeri. Interrogation of the accused led investigators to Mr. Badusha and other members of the network.
Police said the gang sourced and stored large quantities of MDMA in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru before transporting them for distribution in Keralam and Tamil Nadu.

Luxury cars fitted with concealed compartments were allegedly used to move the drugs to transit points, including Coimbatore, Palani and Kodaikanal, before smaller consignments were delivered to different locations.

Investigators identified Mr. Badusha as a key intermediary for the network in Malappuram. Police said that more than 200 kg of MDMA had been smuggled into Keralam under his leadership over the past six months.

Another alleged kingpin, Akhil Joy, a native of Wayanad and a close associate of Mr. Badusha, was arrested from Bihar about a month ago. Mr. Badusha is also an accused in cases involving murder, drug trafficking and theft in Wayanad and Malappuram districts, police said.

After the investigation began, Mr. Badusha allegedly went into hiding in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Odisha and Chennai. Bengaluru Police were also looking for him after he reportedly abandoned a car in Electronic City following a collision involving around 10 vehicles.

The special investigation team (SIT), including officers from the Malappuram and Perinthalmanna police sub-divisions, the Narcotics Cell and the District Anti-Narcotic Special Action Force (DANSAF), carried out the arrest.
Police said the investigation was continuing to trace the source of the drugs and identify other members of the network.

articles.title: Kannur panchayat contracts: KSU vice-president challenges allegations, threatens legal action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kerala Students Union (KSU) State vice-president P. Muhammed Shammas has challenged Carton India Alliance Private Limited managing director Mohammed Asif to produce evidence for the allegations against him and threatened legal action, escalating the controversy over alleged irregularities in contracts awarded by the Kannur district panchayat.

The confrontation comes amid a fresh vigilance investigation into alleged irregularities in public works contracts worth more than ₹12 crore awarded to the company. The Keralam government sanctioned the investigation on October 23 against former district panchayat president P.P. Divya, her husband V.P. Ajith and former district panchayat secretary Abdul Latheef, following a complaint by Mr. Shammas. The probe was authorised under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Addressing the media in Kannur, Mr. Shammas said he had been raising allegations of corruption and benami transactions for nearly two years and had submitted complaints and supporting documents to the authorities.
Responding to allegations that he had sought money through an intermediary, he said the claims had changed from an initial allegation of a demand for money to one involving ₹5 lakh.

“Let them not think that they can divert the issue by raising such cheap allegations. I have placed the matters before the public and the authorities with documents and evidence. I challenge Mohammed Asif to produce the evidence on which his allegations against me are based,” he said.
Mr. Shammas said he would initiate legal action against Mr. Asif over what he described as a malicious campaign.

Mr. Shammas questioned the relationship between Ms. Divya and Carton India Alliance, as well as Mr. Asif’s association with the company. He referred to audio recordings and WhatsApp screenshots that he claimed raised questions about their alleged links.

He cited a voice message in which Mr. Asif allegedly asked someone to meet Binoy Kurian, then district panchayat vice-president, reportedly at Ms. Divya’s direction. Mr. Shammas said the recordings and related material had been brought to the attention of the authorities, including the Vigilance department.

Responding to the allegations, Mr. Kurian denied that contracts had been awarded without following tender procedures. He said the district panchayat had invited tenders from project management consultants in 2022-23, with three companies participating and SILK being selected for quoting the lowest percentage charge.
SILK subsequently prepared estimates and invited tenders to select executing agencies, including Carton India Alliance, he said.

“The district panchayat has no role in selecting Carton India. That responsibility rests with SILK,” Mr. Kurian said, adding that the prescribed procedures had been followed and the relevant files were available for public scrutiny at the district panchayat office.

articles.title: Madras High Court denies anticipatory bail to Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in ₹100-crore private schools fraud case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Madras High Court on Monday (October 26, 2026) denied anticipatory bail to former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi of the DMK in a corruption case after observing that the final destination of over ₹400 crore, allegedly collected towards a ‘party fund’ from over 177 private school managements in the State, could be found out only if he is subjected to custodial interrogation.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan said he was of the view that grant of advance bail to the former Minister would paralyse the investigation being conducted by the Central Crime Branch for offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

“While protection of individual liberty is a duty of the court, it should be weighed against the society’s need for a corruption-free governmental administration,” he said. Rejecting the petitioner’s argument that all evidence in the case was documentary in nature, and hence, his arrest was not absolutely necessary in such a case, the judge said: “Money trails would still require custodial interrogation in order to establish the intent and identify who had been holding the strings and the final destination of the amount alleged to be involved.”

Further, the judge recorded the submission of State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan that the second accused Muthukumar, who was a classmate of the former Minister and also the treasurer of a private schools association through which the ‘party fund’ was collected, was still absconding and his whereabouts could be found out only by interrogating the present petitioner. “The petitioner is a politician, holding a high position. If anticipatory bail is granted before the second accused is apprehended, then it would become a tool for the second accused to avoid the process of the investigation. As the investigation is still at its nascent stage and as new facts are being unearthed, this court is of the view that grant of anticipatory bail would not be fit and proper,” Justice Lakshminarayanan said.

He went on to state that corruption was a grave economic offence. “It not only affects the public exchequer but is also a crime against humanity and directly affects the human rights. In cases such as these, the court has to keep in mind the position that had been occupied by the petitioner and thereby his ability to tamper with the State machineries or influence witnesses.”

He also said courts would generally be slow in granting anticipatory bail in corruption cases, especially when a strong apprehension arose that the petitioner could use the liberty to influence witnesses, hamper investigation, or destroy physical evidence. “In the present case, prima facie, the records reveal that the absconding accused — A2 has been shielded by the petitioner,” he wrote.

The judge said Justices J.B. Pardiwala and R. Mahadevan of the Supreme Court had in 2025 held that in corruption cases, anticipatory bail could not be sought as a matter of right, and it could be granted only in cases involving political vendetta, false implications, or manifest frivolity. “None of the exceptions pointed out by Pardiwala J. applies to the facts of the present case,” he concluded.

According to the CCB, the first and second accused were the founder president and treasurer respectively of an unregistered body titled ‘Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association’. They were instrumental in collecting crores of rupees from various private school managements for purposes such as gaining permanent recognition, upgradation , DTCP/CMDA approvals, building related permissions and other government approvals.
Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi arrested in ₹100-crore private schools fraud case
Investigation reveals collection of ‘party fund’ during Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi’s tenure as School Education Minister, CCB tells Madras High Court

The investigating agency claimed the unregistered association was formed in 2024 on the basis of the former Minister’s communication through his personal assistant Valadi Karthick. Mr. Poyyamozhi had participated in the event held for inaugurating the association at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024. Claiming that it had secured the video footage of the event, the CCB said, the then Minister had “projected” Mr. Arasakumar and Mr. Muthukumar before a large gathering of school correspondents.

Thereafter, all the needs of individual school managements were routed through the first two accused for being placed before the higher government level. So far, “more than 177 victim school managements have come forward and a prima facie amount of ₹17,26,73,650 has been traced. The complete financial trail and ultimate beneficiaries is still under investigation,” the CCB told the court.

articles.title: Virtual autopsy at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital: launch likely to take time
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposed launch of virtual autopsy (virtopsy), an advanced forensic technique, at the Government Medical College Hospital (MCH), Kozhikode, is likely to take some more time as the work in this regard is still in progress.

According to official sources, one of the members from the Department of Forensic Medicine at the hospital recently underwent a month-long training in the subject at the North-Eastern Hill Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences, Shillong, Meghalaya, which is a pioneer in virtual autopsy in the country.

The department has also submitted a detailed list of the facilities to be introduced at the hospital, including the staff to be appointed and the equipment to be installed, to the government. The sources said that discussions are also ongoing with experts at the All-India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi.

The main objectives of an autopsy are determining the cause and manner of death, establishing identity, and collecting evidence for litigation and investigation. Virtual autopsy reports are almost identical to traditional autopsy reports, the difference is only in the use of advanced imaging instead of invasive dissection. Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) technologies are used for this non-invasive procedure, where three-dimensional data of the entire body, or relevant parts, are created to examine the details. However, forensic experts point out that in suspicious or unnatural deaths, a medico-legal autopsy is always mandatory.

According to Health department sources, none of the government hospitals in Keralam follows such a system at present. A.K. Unmesh, Professor, Forensic Medicine, had given a detailed project report (DPR) to the government in December 2025 to set up a virtual autopsy centre at the Government Medical College, Kottayam, where he was working then as the Head of the Department. The DPR had said that setting up such a facility would improve medico-legal services, enhance judicial transparency, reduce the stress of families by offering minimally invasive options, and provide permanent digital evidence for appeals and reviews. The plan was to enhance collaboration between departments such as Radiology and Forensic Medicine, and the judiciary and law enforcement. It was also pointed out that a digital repository of forensic imaging could be created for evidence and academic research. The total projected capital cost was ₹15.5 crore, and the recurring annual cost was estimated to be ₹2.5 crore.
After the United Democratic Front (UDF) came to power in May this year, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has repeatedly declared that the virtual autopsy system would be first launched in Kozhikode.

articles.title: BPCL shifts crude sourcing towards Middle East as Russian oil loses price edge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) tapped more into Middle Eastern crude as Russian oil lost its price advantage and also due to rising freight costs, with the shift becoming more pronounced in November, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, Director (Finance), told analysts during a post-results call on Monday.

“Our spot crude share remained at around 67% in the second quarter, while Russian grade accounted for approximately 37% of our total crude procurement, both broadly in line with the previous quarter,” Mr. Gupta said, adding that the company increased purchases from the Middle East as supplies from the region improved.

Russia accounted for 37% of BPCL’s crude basket in the September quarter, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19%, Abu Dhabi at 17%, the U.S. at 9% and Oman at 6%. The remaining supplies came from countries contributing 1-4% each.
As of September-end, BPCL held about 22 days of crude inventory, with sourcing requirements tied up through December.
Mr. Gupta said the share of Russian crude in October was expected to remain “more or less the same”, although procurement volumes would be lower for November.

“October, our requirement from Russia slightly came down but in the month of November, the cargoes from Russia significantly reduced due to [reduced] commercial viability [compared to that from Middle East], mainly the increase in the freight,” he said, adding that the company did not receive attractive offers for Russian crude in November.

Russian crude was available at a premium of $12-$13 per barrel over benchmark prices in October. The premium has narrowed to $1-$2 per barrel for December cargoes, Mr. Gupta said, although freight costs remain high.
“Maybe today, Russian cargo is preferable than a Middle Eastern cargo for December month because November [procurement] we have already concluded,” he said.

BPCL also diversified its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sourcing during the quarter. Supplies from the Arab Gulf improved, while the US accounted for about 48% of LPG imports in the September quarter.
Softening Saudi Contract Prices (Saudi CP), the benchmark for LPG pricing, helped reduce under-recoveries to an average ₹290 per cylinder in the September quarter from ₹507 in the June quarter.

Under-recoveries are expected to be ₹245 per cylinder in October and are expected to rise to ₹328 in November, Mr. Gupta said. BPCL currently holds 32 days of LPG inventory, including supplies in transit.
The company has also diversified liquefied natural gas (LNG) procurement by increasing spot purchases from the US, Oman and West Africa.

articles.title: Rubio to host G20 Foreign Ministers’ meet in Atlanta on Oct 30-31
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting this weekend in Atlanta to strengthen efforts to advance practical cooperation on shared economic and security challenges, thereby setting the stage for the leaders’ meeting in December.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is scheduled to attend the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta on October 30-31.

“Under President Trump's leadership, the United States is returning the G20 to its core economic mission of driving growth, strengthening economic security, and delivering results for the American people,” the Department of State said in a statement.
It said Mr. Rubio will convene Foreign Ministers from the world’s leading economies to advance practical cooperation on shared economic and security challenges.

“Throughout the ministerial, the United States will work with G20 partners to address geopolitical crises contributing to global economic shocks, including threats to freedom of navigation, energy and food security, and supply chains,” the State Department said.

It said global security and economic prosperity are inextricably linked, and these discussions will set the stage for U.S. President Trump’s G20 Leaders’ Summit and the broader economic agenda that leaders will tackle.

As a global hub of diplomacy, connectivity, and commerce, Atlanta offers the perfect backdrop for these discussions. U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to host the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Miami on December 14-15.

articles.title: Anthropic files for IPO as revenue jumps 14-fold to $16.3 billion in H1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, has filed to go public in the United States, disclosing rapid revenue growth, expanding enterprise spending and the high cost of developing and running advanced AI models.

The company filed a registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 26. It intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The number of shares to be offered and the price range have not yet been determined.
The public filing follows Anthropic’s confidential submission of a draft registration statement to the SEC on June 1, 2026. The proposed IPO remains subject to regulatory review.

One of the key disclosures is that revenue from a group of existing customers was about nine times higher in the three months ended September 30, 2026, than in the same period a year earlier. The calculation includes customers who generated at least $1 in revenue in the earlier period but excludes subscribers to Anthropic’s Claude Pro and Max plans.

The company reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September 30, up from more than 950 a year earlier. More than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million, while approximately 250 generated at least $10 million.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. Its net loss widened to $80.7 billion from $13 billion, largely because of accounting expenses arising from changes in the estimated value of certain financing instruments as the company’s valuation rose.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, compared with $2.14 billion a year earlier. However, using its own adjusted measure, which excludes certain expenses, the company reported operating income of $1.6 billion, with a margin of about 10%.

It reported $8.95 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses in the first half of 2026, reflecting the costs of developing and running advanced AI models. As of June 30, the company held $131.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, according to the filing.

The prospectus flags risks including dependence on computing infrastructure providers, competition and the cost of developing increasingly capable AI models. Major cloud providers supply Anthropic with computing capacity and help distribute its products, while also developing competing AI services.

The filing also outlines a governance structure intended to protect Anthropic’s long-term public-benefit mission. An entity formed by its seven co-founders will hold a special share carrying 50.1% of general voting power, while the company’s Long-Term Benefit Trust will have the right to appoint a majority of the board. This would limit the ability of ordinary shareholders to influence corporate governance, even after the company lists publicly.
Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the proposed price range. The timing and terms of the IPO will depend on the regulatory process and market conditions.

articles.title: Russia says open to mini Ukraine ceasefires, but no letup in war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Russia said Monday (October 26, 2026) that it would not slow down its offensive on Ukraine despite upcoming U.S.-brokered talks on ending the conflict but that it could agree local "humanitarian" ceasefires.
The Kremlin said that it was open to short-term "humanitarian" ceasefires along the front line, ahead of a truce in the ravaged Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

A ceasefire is to start in the southern Ukrainian city early Tuesday (October 27), brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump after months of reports that residents faced dire food, water and medicine shortages.
Asked whether Russia would consider more local truces, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters: "For humanitarian purposes, absolutely."
But Moscow vowed not to let up in the overall pace of the war, even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under U.S. mediation next month.
"The decision to resume trilateral talks does not imply any restrictions on combat operations," Mr. Peskov said.
"Our armed forces continue to carry out massive strikes on Ukraine's military-industrial complex," he added.

Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, hitting energy sites around major cities in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.
Strikes last year left millions without heating or electricity with temperatures as low as -20C.
The two sides are to meet next month with U.S. envoys to discuss ways to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II.
Several previous rounds have failed to move the sides closer to a deal. Russia demands more territory in eastern Ukraine and sweeping military and political restrictions on Kyiv.
Ukraine and its allies say the demands are tantamount to a capitulation that would leave the country exposed to a future Russian attack.
